stem: A worker records several observations at the end of shift but labels them as if entered at the original observation times. What data-integrity problem is created?
choices: The entries falsely appear contemporaneous even though they were recorded later from memory, obscuring the actual timing of data capture.
The entries are unreliable mainly because end-of-shift handwriting tends to be more uniform than real-time entries.
Paper observations become invalid automatically if they are not entered into an electronic system immediately.
There is no integrity concern if the worker remembers the observations accurately and the values are plausible.
rationale: Retrospective entry is not automatically prohibited, but it must be represented truthfully. Recording later observations as though they were written at the original time makes the record appear contemporaneous when it was not and hides reliance on memory. The actual recording time and retrospective nature should be documented according to procedure.
